SessionStart._comment: startup and resume ONLY. SessionStart also fires on 'compact', 'clear' and 'fork' — all of which happen mid-conversation on the SAME machine, where there is nothing to restore. Pulling then is at best wasted work and at worst writes over files the running session is using.

SessionEnd._comment: Hooks fire PER CONVERSATION, not per client. Several conversations ending together means several concurrent pushes at one remote, so cli.mjs takes a lock and later arrivals no-op rather than race. 'clear' is excluded: clearing context is not finishing work, and it would push on every /clear. 'resume' is ALSO excluded here (confirmed against Claude Code's hooks docs: SessionEnd 'resume' = 'session paused for resume', a real value, not a typo) -- resuming a conversation fires SessionEnd(resume) on the OLD session and SessionStart(resume) on the NEW one within the same fraction of a second, and the old session is not actually finishing: the SAME transcript is immediately picked back up by the resumed session, which will fire its own genuine SessionEnd later. Pushing here bought nothing but a guaranteed lock collision with the concurrent auto-pull -- live log showed a pull/push/pull triplet inside 0.7s, and 91 'skipped' log lines against only 18 'push ok' across the whole history. Dropped 2026-09-07.
